speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I need to understand the progression of your symptoms: do you have trouble climbing stairs and experiencing upper limb weakness alongside your double vision, and how long have these issues been present?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you describe—diplopia on vertical gaze, weakness worsening with activity and improving with rest, and the absence of sensory or balance issues—are highly suggestive of a specific neuromuscular disorder. To confirm this, I need to see your eye movements and measure your muscle strength. REQUEST IMAGES: Eye_movement_video; REQUEST TEST: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation.

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Eye_movement_video: Presence of ptosis (drooping of the right upper eyelid) that worsens with sustained upward gaze, consistent with diplopia on vertical gaze. Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The clinical presentation of fatigable weakness worsening with activity, ptosis worsening with upward gaze, and confirmed electrophysiological findings of decreased muscle response on repetitive nerve stimulation confirm this diagnosis.
